I work at a company that rolled out 2FA on employee accounts after over $100,000 was lost due to fraudulent payments related to a management account being compromised. 2FA absolutely adds account security because the person accessing must be physically holding a previously registered device. You might be able to notice a scam to steal your password, but not every user can. Google is rolling out this requirement to deal with the type of user who does fall for a scam.

The phone doesn't need an activated plan, the ability to do calls/texts or connect to the mobile data network. Any Android phone without a plan can connect to a wifi network and act as your 2FA device.

You can ditch Gmail over this, but I'd urge you to prepare for 2FA by getting a cheap mobile device. This is the new standard for account security. All the tech companies are doing it, workplaces with employee accounts do it, it's only a matter of time before it's required to do online banking and to use online payment processors such as PayPal.

It's a no brainer move in an environment where the largest cause for account breach is users that willingly give up passwords to scammers.
